stem.text: When a sample of a radioactive isotope decays by $\alpha$-particle emission, the $\alpha$-particles emitted have a single discrete energy.
When a sample of a radioactive isotope decays by $\beta^{-}$ particle emission, the $\beta^{-}$ particles emitted have a continuous range of energies.
What is the explanation for this?

A.text: An antineutrino is emitted with a $\beta^{-}$ particle but not with an $\alpha$-particle.

B.text: An antineutrino is emitted with an $\alpha$-particle but not with a $\beta^{-}$ particle.

C.text: The $\alpha$-particles have much more energy than the $\beta^{-}$ particles.

D.text: The $\beta^{-}$ particles have much more energy than the $\alpha$-particles.
